editorNote: A quiet-sky week with a lot of motion: a suspected planet built from a dead star's debris, a record-fast ride to the space station, a Nobel for catching neutrinos from deep space, and a military-satellite launch that keeps slipping.

stories.headline: Hubble archive hints at a second-generation planet around a white dwarf
stories.summary: Reanalysing 1999 Hubble data, a Warwick-led team found unusually abundant niobium around the white dwarf HS 0209+0832 and argues it points to a Jupiter-sized planet built from material the dying star shed, orbiting about 3.7 million miles out. NASA calls the planet suspected, not confirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: If it holds up, it would be a rare planet formed after its star died; for now the evidence is chemical and the formation story is a model.

sourceLinks.title: Suspected Second-generation Planet Solves NASA Hubble Cold Case (NASA Science)
Astronomers Solve Cosmic Cold Case with NASA Hubble Data (NASA)

stories.headline: Crew-13 docks at the station less than eight hours after launch, the fastest for a U.S. spacecraft
stories.summary: Following the October 1 liftoff we reported, Dragon reached the International Space Station in under eight hours. NASA had billed the plan as the fastest launch-to-docking for a U.S. spacecraft in the station's history.
stories.whyItMatters: The four-person Crew-13 team is now aboard, bringing the station to 11 people during handover.

sourceLinks.title: NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 Secured Inside Dragon, Ready for Hatch Closure (NASA)
SpaceX Crew-13 astronauts dock at ISS less than 8 hours after launch (Space.com)

stories.headline: Francis Halzen wins the Nobel Prize in Physics for IceCube and high-energy cosmic neutrinos
stories.summary: The Royal Swedish Academy honoured Halzen on October 6 for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.
stories.whyItMatters: It recognises neutrinos from beyond Earth as a working way to observe the universe.

sourceLinks.title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 awarded to Francis Halzen (Free Press Journal)

stories.headline: SDA's fourth Tranche 1 launch slips again, now targeting October 10
stories.summary: A Falcon 9 carrying 21 Space Development Agency data-transport satellites auto-aborted just before liftoff from Vandenberg on October 5; SpaceX said vehicle and payload were healthy. The target has since moved from October 8 to 9 and now to a window early on October 10.
stories.whyItMatters: The launch is part of a military communications and missile-warning constellation, and it is still on the pad.

sourceLinks.title: SpaceX to launch SDA's fourth Tranche 1 data transport mission (KSBY)
